question: In a driving simulator, which conversation hurt driving more: one with a passenger, or one on a hands-free phone?
answer: The hands-free phone call. Drews, Pasupathi and Strayer asked talking drivers to leave the motorway at a rest stop. Those on the phone missed the exit far more often. A passenger sees the road too, pausing the talk when traffic thickens and sometimes pointing out the exit. The caller talks on, blind to the lorry.
move: A helper who shares the view is worth more than one who shares the words.
ask: When I need help while concentrating, who shares my view rather than just my words?
trap: Neither, since a conversation seems equally demanding wherever the other person sits.
reference: Drews, Pasupathi & Strayer, Passenger and cell phone conversations in simulated driving, Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied, 2008
